hook: He painted The Starry Night and Sunflowers, and is said to have sold just one painting in his life.

pages.x: Vincent van Gogh was born in 1853 in Zundert, in the Netherlands, the son of a pastor. He worked for art dealers in The Hague, London and Paris, but was sacked, and tried to become a preacher.
In 1879 he preached to coal miners in the Borinage, in Belgium, gave away his clothes and slept on straw. The church dismissed him for being too extreme. At 27 he decided to become an artist.
His early paintings were dark pictures of peasants and weavers. In 1885 in Nuenen he painted a poor family eating potatoes by lamplight, with hands, he said, that had dug the earth.
His younger brother Theo, an art dealer in Paris, sent him money all his life, and Vincent wrote him more than 600 letters. In Paris he met the Impressionists, and his colours turned bright.
In 1888 he moved to Arles, in the south of France, dazzled by its light. He painted Sunflowers to decorate the room for his friend, the painter Paul Gauguin, who came to stay.
Van Gogh suffered from mental illness. In December 1888, after a quarrel with Gauguin, he had a breakdown and cut off his left ear with a razor. Gauguin left Arles.
In 1889 he chose to go into a hospital at Saint-Rémy. From his window he painted The Starry Night, with swirling stars and a crescent moon over a sleeping village.

In ten years he made about 2,100 works, among them some 860 oil paintings, most of them in his last two years. In July 1890, at Auvers, he died of a gunshot wound, most likely by his own hand. He was 37.
Van Gogh's bold colours and swirling brushstrokes made him one of the most famous painters who ever lived. His paintings now sell for tens of millions.
